concept: Atlas for Government regions and cloud providers
summary: Source-anchored research for Atlas for Government regions and cloud providers. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: The AtlasGov region guide requires the `_AW` suffix when supplying a Google Cloud region name to the Atlas API, including through Terraform; the guide gives `US_EAST_1_AW` as its example. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

AtlasGov requires a standard-region or government-region designation when creating a project; clusters cannot span government and standard regions within the same project. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

The AtlasGov project guide makes Google Cloud available only in government-region-use projects. A standard-region project can deploy AWS clusters only to standard regions and cannot deploy other cloud providers. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Google’s Assured Workloads Americas table lists these US resource locations: Iowa (`us-central1`), South Carolina (`us-east1`), Northern Virginia (`us-east4`), Ohio (`us-east5`), Texas (`us-south1`), Oregon (`us-west1`), Los Angeles (`us-west2`), Salt Lake City (`us-west3`), and Las Vegas (`us-west4`). This is Google’s underlying location list, rather than a tested enumeration of AtlasGov API region values. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-26)

AtlasGov lists AWS GovCloud Northwestern US (us-gov-west-1) and Eastern US (us-gov-east-1), plus AWS commercial Northern Virginia (us-east-1), Ohio (us-east-2), Northern California (us-west-1), and Oregon (us-west-2). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

MongoDB documents AtlasGov deployment in Google Cloud with Assured Workloads in all standard US regions and directs readers to Google’s Assured Workloads locations table for the region list. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
AtlasGov permits multi-region clusters, but the cluster-creation guide forbids a deployment spanning government and standard regions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14)

Pulumi states an AWS-only provider restriction; MongoDB project documentation explicitly describes GCP availability. The AWS-only statement conflicts with MongoDB documentation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
The AtlasGov supported-region guide lists AWS GovCloud, AWS commercial US regions, and Google Cloud with Assured Workloads as deployment options. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
AtlasGov supports AWS GovCloud Northwestern US (`us-gov-west-1`) and Eastern US (`us-gov-east-1`). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

AtlasGov supports AWS commercial standard regions Northern Virginia (`us-east-1`), Ohio (`us-east-2`), Northern California (`us-west-1`), and Oregon (`us-west-2`). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)
